_note: ROUND 4 placement map for room 5 (Living Room). All coordinates are ROOM-LOCAL feet from the footprint's min corner -- exactly what roomkit.place takes. Read tools/roomkit/ROOM-BRIEF.md first. Pieces are authored facing +z (south); rot then aims them: 0 = back to the NORTH wall, 90 = back to the WEST wall, 180 = back to the SOUTH wall, 270 = back to the EAST wall. Round-4 build scripts live in scratchpad/lr5/ (kit4.py + b4_shell/b4_focal/b4_soft/b4_accents/b4_shadows.py, shot set in shots4.py, patch meter in m.py, wall probe in wallprobe.py); each is idempotent and re-runnable and each supersedes its b3_* twin. kit4 imports kit3 which imports kit2 for the edge/sweep/placement helpers. Round 4 was a SURFACES AND SOFT GOODS round only: the inventory, scale and layout were adjudicated correct in round 3 and were not touched. b3_view.py (outdoor boards) and b3_shell.py's ceiling/baseboards are still the live source for those pieces -- b4_shell.py only re-tones the walls.

_room_surfaces.note: ROUND 4 RE-TONED, and this time all four walls were metered. Round 3 shipped #979693 and reported 'average 169, in the photo's range'; a critic re-metered and found that averaged only the two brightest walls. The honest round-3 numbers, from CLEAN patches verified against a _boxes.png overlay: north 194.3 / west 134.0 / east 98.2 / south 72.3, average 124.7. wallprobe.py then took a second point at #c9c8c4 (221.8/177.7/142.8/112.6, average 163.7), giving per-wall slopes of 0.55 (N) / 0.87 (W) / 0.89 (E) / 0.81 (S) render bytes per albedo byte. #c0bfbb lands north 218.1 / west 171.0 / east 135.4 / south 105.5, AVERAGE 157.5, against photo f's four clean wall patches at 157.1 / 159.6 / 176.7 / 147.6 (mean 160.3, range 148-177). The 113-byte wall-to-wall spread is the renderer's one-sun-no-bounce limit (ROOM-BRIEF: 'a known limit, not your bug') and is now WORSE in absolute terms than at #979693, because the bright walls respond less than the dark ones; that is the arithmetic consequence of aiming at the average, which is what the brief asks for. Ceiling stays emissive-driven (#c4c4c4) because a downward-facing plane collects essentially no light in this scene.

Living Fireplace.note: White PAINTED FIELDSTONE breast on the chamfer, floor to ceiling. ROUND 4 REBUILT THE STONE SURFACE (the count was adjudicated correct, the material was not). Round 3 metered sd 34.2 at mean 205 against photo f's 8.1 / 171-185, because it put a dark recessed joint (#a6a39e) behind bevelled pillows: the pillow rims face sideways, catch no light, and drew a black outline round every stone. Round 4: (a) the joint lifts to #9a978f, within ~5% of the stone family, and the gap narrows to a 0.026 ft shrink; (b) each stone is a `plate` (kit4) -- a FLAT angular cap with its own small random tilt, 0.036-0.058 ft proud of the joint plane -- instead of a three-ring dome, because photo_stonecrop.png shows flat painted plates with thin seams and essentially no within-stone gradient; (c) seeds are laid in COURSES 0.85 ft tall with widths varying ~3:1 (`coursed_seeds`), giving 63 stones on the 6.86 x 9.0 face with a horizontal grain instead of near-equant crazy paving. Metered on three CLEAN patches verified against a _boxes overlay: 186.9 / 188.9 / 189.6, sd 5.5-6.0, against photo f's 185.3 sd 8.9 over a 2 ft field (178-189, sd 5.7-11.5 over 1 ft patches). Firebox GLASS also rebuilt (item 6): #1d2025 at metallic 0.55 has almost no diffuse term and nothing to reflect, so it metered luminance 5-15 -- a hole in the room. Now #3b414a at metallic 0.05 with three pale reflected streaks: 81.0 mean / sd 32.8 / range 21-178, against photo f's 94.4 / 26.9 / 23-142. Everything else (stepped cast-iron surround, projecting hood, ash lip, log bed, raised stone hearth, mantel, wreath) is round 3's, confirmed good; the wreath was thinned 80 -> 55 leaf plates purely for payload. Placement: objects.js seats a model on its BBOX centre and the mantel/wreath reach further into the room than the chase depth, so the script pushes out by half the MEASURED bbox depth along the chamfer's inward normal.

ROUND 4 (item 7): round 3's ground was #c6c3bd on a #cfcbc3 frame and metered 89 against an east wall of 98 -- a panel painted the wall's own value, with no visible frame. The ground is now #f6f4ef at roughness 0.42 and the frame a slim #2f3033 border: metered 182.6 against a wall of 135.8, i.e. it reads as a white canvas with an outline. Living Floor Rug.note: Flatweave, 13.2 x 11.0 of pile with a bound edge. ROUND 4 REBUILT IT TWICE OVER (item 5). Round 2 overshot with raised ribs; round 3 undershot with a flat +/-1.5% mosaic that metered sd 2.0 against photo f's 20-25, and wrote it as 4453 flat-shaded `box()`es for a file of 4.50 MB -- three times the whole ROOM budget. It is now (a) a base slab, (b) a coarse 0.58 ft tonal mottle at +/-5, and (c) 1350 thin CROSSHATCH streaks (0.024-0.050 ft thick, 0.55-2.20 ft long, six tones at +/-13), which is what photo_rugcrop.png actually shows: long light and dark slubs running both ways over a mid ground. Every quad is 4 SMOOTH verts instead of a 36-vert flat box, so the same field costs 227 KB. Metered on the reference pose: 133.7 sd 20.5 / 136.4 sd 12.8 / 141.3 sd 8.3, against photo f's three clean patches at 131.1 sd 19.8 / 148.7 sd 17.1 / 120.9 sd 21.9. THE TWO 'SEAMS SPLITTING THE RUG INTO PANELS' WERE NOT THE RUG: they were the hard-edged solid CORE of the contact-shadow decals lying on it (see Living Floor Shadows). pos.y = 0.004, NOT 0.010: house.js draws the room slab at y 0.01. NAMED 'Floor Rug' ON PURPOSE so objects.js SURFACE_RE makes it scenery.

Living Floor Shadows.note: One decal object holding a contact shadow under every piece that meets the floor. Round 3's falloff -- nine NON-OVERLAPPING ANNULI per piece, each painted with its own absolute alpha off a smooth curve (a0 0.58, gamma 1.5, pad 1.0 ft), all at ONE y -- was confirmed good and is unchanged. ROUND 4 CHANGED ONE THING: `smooth_shadow4` (kit4) makes the solid CORE optional, and the coffee table's wide ambient halo now starts faded. That core was a hard-edged 3.4 x 1.7 ft rectangle of 22% black lying on the rug under an OPEN X-frame, and its boundary is the horizontal 'hard seam' the round-3 critic read as a tonal panel in the rug. Footprints were also re-fitted to the pieces that moved (both east sofas, the chaise ottoman). NOTE FOR ANYONE TEMPTED TO COMPOSITE INSTEAD: stacking translucent layers to build a gradient does NOT work here -- the layers must sit within a thousandth of a foot of each other to stay under the furniture, which is below the depth buffer's precision at room scale. Annuli cannot be clipped as a ring, so every triangle is Sutherland-Hodgman clipped to the room polygon individually. FOOTPRINTS ARE HAND-COPIED from the build scripts: re-run b4_shadows.py whenever a piece moves.

_what_changed_in_round_4: STONE MATERIAL (item 1): joint #a6a39e -> #9a978f (within ~5% of the stone), gap narrowed, and the three-ring domed pillow replaced by a FLAT tilted `plate` with the joint plane behind it. Clean lit field went 205 mean / sd 34.2 -> 187-190 mean / sd 5.5-6.0 against photo f's 185.3 / 8.9. Seeds re-laid in 0.85 ft COURSES with 3:1 width variation: 63 stones with a horizontal grain.

WALLS (item 2): #979693 (N 194 / W 134 / E 98 / S 72, average 124.7) -> #c0bfbb (N 218.1 / W 171.0 / E 135.4 / S 105.5, average 157.5) against photo f's 148-177, mean 160.3. Picked from a two-point probe, not by eye. All four walls reported.

SOFT GOODS (item 3 + 8): a new `puff` primitive -- a rounded CUBE, smooth-shaded, with an optional per-vertex `nub` -- replaces `rounded_box` on every cushion, arm, back rail and pillow in the room. Silhouettes are plump instead of planar-chamfered, and the nub is a ~0.2 ft shading mottle that stands in for boucle. Added: the sherpa throw + body pillow on the armchair, a rolled tan throw on the north east sofa, a cream body pillow on the south east sofa, weave decks on both ottomans.

EAST SOFAS (item 4): were the same mesh mirrored with a 0.95 ft slot. Now 6.20 x 3.55 / square arms / 3 seats to the north and 6.40 x 3.95 / rolled arms / 2 seats / taller back to the south, touching at 0.15 ft. Ticking stripes now follow the pillow's curve instead of floating in front of it; the floating throw plane on the south sofa was deleted (photo f shows none).

RUG (item 5): flat +/-1.5% panels (sd 2.0) -> a 0.58 ft mottle plus 1350 crosshatch streaks, metering 133.7 / sd 20.5 against photo f's 131.1 / sd 19.8. File 4.50 MB -> 227 KB by writing 4-vert SMOOTH quads instead of 36-vert flat boxes.

THE RUG'S TWO 'HARD SEAMS' were the contact-shadow decal, not the rug: the coffee table's wide ambient halo was drawn with a hard-edged solid core at 22% black over an open X-frame. `smooth_shadow4` makes the core optional and that halo now starts faded. The nine-annulus falloff itself is untouched.

FIREBOX GLASS (item 6): #1d2025 at metallic 0.55 metered 5-15 (a hole in the room) -> #3b414a at metallic 0.05 with three reflected streaks, 81.0 mean / sd 32.8 / range 21-178, against photo f's 94.4 / 26.9 / 23-142.

ART EAST (item 7): mid-grey ground on a same-value frame (89 against a 98 wall) -> near-white ground on a slim dark frame (182.6 against a 135.8 wall), and the black mass rebuilt as one organic blob polygon instead of four stacked boxes.
PAYLOAD: room 5 went from ~6.4 MB to 1.833 MB, and the whole house from 26 MB to 19 MB. Largest piece is now 233 KB (was 4.50 MB).
DOLLHOUSE POSE: doll_nw, not doll_se -- see camera_ref.dollhouse_pose.
_disagreements: ART EAST'S RATIO. The finding asked for a white canvas because round 3's read as a panel. Photo f's canvas ground (152-155) is however about EQUAL to its east wall (148-177), so matching the photo's canvas/wall RATIO in this render (east wall 135) would put the canvas back at ~135 and reproduce the fault. The canvas was aimed at reading white (182.6 vs 135.8, ratio 1.34) rather than at the photo ratio (0.96). If a future critic prefers the ratio, drop CANVAS_E from #f6f4ef to about #b8b5af.

STONE vs NORTH WALL. Photo f has the stone BRIGHTER than its adjacent north wall (185 vs 157, ratio 1.18). Aiming the four-wall average at the photo (item 2) puts the render's north wall at 218, so the render now has the stone DARKER than that wall (188 vs 218, ratio 0.86) even though both surfaces individually meter the photo's value. The two asks are not simultaneously satisfiable while the renderer's wall-to-wall spread is 113 bytes; item 2 was treated as the binding one.

PAYLOAD. 1.833 MB against the 1.5 MB target. Every piece I built is under the 300 KB piece cap and the room is down 3.5x from round 3. The residual sits in pieces round 3's critic confirmed good and this round was told not to disturb: Living Floor Shadows 233 KB, Living Ceiling 102 KB, the three Outdoor View boards 197 KB, Living Etagere 73 KB, Living Corner Plant 62 KB, Living Basket 57 KB, Living Pet Crate 55 KB. Trimming the three outdoor boards and the shadow decal's ring count from 9 to 7 would land the room at ~1.45 MB.
_known_gaps: Wall-to-wall spread is 112.6 bytes (north 218.1, south 105.5) against a real room's ~17 -- barely better than round 3's 122.0 (194.3 - 72.3). One directional sun, no bounce, one wall_color, emissive banned: ROOM-BRIEF documents this as the renderer's limit. Only the AVERAGE is now in the photo's range, and the north wall (218) is over the photo's ceiling value.

The stone reads a touch brighter than the photo (187-190 vs 178-189 on 1 ft patches) and has essentially no relief left: the plates are flat caps 0.036-0.058 ft proud of the joint plane with no chamfer band. Adding the chamfer back costs 140 KB and pushed the metered sd from 6 to 13-18, so it was traded away for the number the finding named.
The rug has no sun dapple. A large part of photo f's rug variance is sunlight through the slider blinds, which this scene has no mechanism to produce; the crosshatch alone carries the metered sd.
The TV picture is emissive colour fields, not a photograph -- the GLB writer has no textures.
The corner plant sits on a stretch of south wall no photo shows clearly. It is plausible density, not documented furniture.

The outdoor view boards are visible edge-on from doll_nw and doll_ne as coloured slabs standing outside the north and west walls. They were built for the through-the-window view only and were not re-cut this round.

shot.py's flyTo does not fully converge its camera TARGET before the screenshot, so the rendered yaw drifts from the requested one. The ref pose works around it by putting the target 200 ft out along the ray.
